title: One-sided-DIQKD using any pure bipartite entangled state secure against all attacks
authors: Bohnishikha Ghosh, Chithra Raj, Shubhayan Sarkar
abstract: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) allows spatially separated parties to establish a secret key among themselves based on quantum principles. While QKD systems are being deployed worldwide, their reliance on trusted measurements makes them vulnerable. Moreover, existing protocols have largely focussed on the qubit cases, and rely on the maximally entangled state, a costly resource to generate. Here, we consider the one-sided-device-independent (1SDI) QKD protocols, where one of the measurement devices is trusted while the other is untrusted. The resource in this scenario is quantum steering, an asymmetric form of quantum nonlocality. This is inspired by a real-world scenario, where the trusted party can be considered to be a bank, or any large organisation that has sufficient resources to protect its systems and validate them, while the users are vulnerable to attacks. We then demonstrate that a secure key can be obtained using any pure bipartite entangled state in this setup. Considering realistic detectors and sources based on current technology, we demonstrate that even states that are almost separable can be used to extract a secure key. Moreover, for every pure entangled bipartite state, we find the critical detection efficiencies and visibility to obtain a secure key.
summary: This paper analyzes One-sided-Device-Independent Quantum Key Distribution (1SDI-QKD) protocols, addressing vulnerabilities in current QKD systems. It proves that a secure key can be extracted using any pure bipartite entangled state, even when the state is nearly separable. The analysis provides explicit bounds on the key rate based on realistic parameters like detector efficiency and state visibility.
main_problem: To develop Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols secure against attacks when one measurement device is untrusted (1SDI-QKD).
main_result: A secure key can be obtained using any pure bipartite entangled state in the 1SDI setup, and the key rate is robust even for states that are almost separable.
method: The security analysis involves deriving lower bounds on the key rate using information-theoretic measures, such as the Devetak-Winter rate, applied to the joint statistics of measurement outcomes.
model_or_system: The model is the One-sided-Device-Independent (1SDI) QKD scenario, where an untrusted source distributes a bipartite state $ho_{AB}$ between an untrusted Alice and a trusted Bob. Security relies on quantum steering.

paper_structure:
The paper establishes the 1SDI-QKD framework, derives the key rate lower bound for the noiseless case using arbitrary pure entangled states, and then extends this analysis to realistic scenarios incorporating finite detection efficiency ($\eta$) and state visibility ($
u$).
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, resource-efficient protocols for quantum communication, showing that high-quality entanglement is not a prerequisite for secure key generation, which is crucial for practical quantum network deployment.
